A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IWN research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Content can be matched reliably across pagination and section changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations comparing MPNN and 2-IWN outputs on graphs sampled from four graphons. Figures 2–3 report convergence errors and prediction intervals; Appendix H documents the experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original graph-sampling simulations, their results in Figures 2–3, and their experimental details in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The IWN architecture, bounded equivariant operators, refinement-based WNNs, and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same procedures. The two-layer subclass in the new transferability analysis specializes the existing architecture rather than introducing a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Erdős–Rényi, stochastic block, triangular, and narrow graphons with constant node signals, addressing the same convergence and size-transferability questions.

E2.justification: Figures 2–3 and Appendix H retain the same comparison between a mean-aggregation MPNN and a 2-IWN. Newly discussed related methods are not additional evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix H retains 100 sampled graphs per graphon and size, sizes 200–1000, a 1000-node weighted graphon approximation, and two-layer models with hidden dimension 16 and sigmoid activation. The reported evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same convergence-error and output-dispersion analyses. No empirical ablation, sensitivity test, robustness scenario, or case study is added or removed; the new Appendix G material is theoretical.

E5.justification: Both report the same graph-sampling variability through 90% prediction intervals, calculated from the 0.05 and 0.95 output quantiles. Seed, repeated-run, and significance-reporting practices do not change.

E6.justification: The plotted content in Figures 1–3 is identical. Both report decreasing MPNN graphon-limit errors, persistent 2-IWN errors, and contracting output intervals for both models. No empirical result entries are added or changed.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 5.4 and formal Theorem G.1, with a power-series proof of cut-distance Lipschitzness for a restricted two-layer analytic IWN class satisfying a weight/radius condition. Corollary 5.3 broadens v1's integral factorization to arbitrary continuous functions of WL distributions, with an additional Stone–Weierstrass argument. Theorem 5.2 is restated as qualitative convergence, while its epsilon-dependent bound remains in the appendix proof.

C1.justification: A central transferability claim is narrowed: v1's abstract and conclusion describe higher-order GNNs as comparably transferable to MPNNs, whereas v2 claims transferability remains achievable. Quantitative guarantees are now presented separately for a restricted IWN class. The expressivity and universal-approximation contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: V1 interprets its general bound as matching MPNN worst-case rates; v2 explicitly says the general theorem provides no rate. Appendix G.4 explains the additional Lipschitz-extension requirement and discusses analytic activation and weight restrictions, impractical parametrization, potentially large and loose constants, and unresolved multilayer extensions.

D1.justification: Appendix H retains the same setup disclosures, repository link, and implementation pseudocode. Renaming the forward-pass symbols does not change the reproducibility information or procedures.

R1.justification: V2 adds Keriven et al. (2020) and Klopp and Verzelen (2019), expands discussion of the already cited node-ID-based universal GNN work, and reframes the diagonal issue in Cai and Wang through self-looped graph limits. Most other reference edits update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites the transferability narrative, combines corollaries, reorganizes Appendix G, expands notation explanations, and standardizes references and affiliation markers. The overall section structure and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and both tables are retained. Figure 5's diagram styling and spacing change, Table 1 gains notation entries, and figures shift with text reflow. The bibliography is condensed; the empirical plots themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 better aligns its general transferability claims with their proof, fixes the WL-readout coverage, and adds a useful conditional Lipschitz theorem. New defects limit the gain: Equation (18) omits the expectation required by its derivation, and Equation (198)'s finite-sample unbiasedness identity conflicts with the simple-graph normalization. For the admissible N(W)=integral W², constant W=1/2 and k=2, its sides are 1/2 and 1/4. These defects do not enter the formal proof of Theorem G.1, but temper the improvements in theoretical precision and scope.
